## Examples {.unnumbered}

### NMDS with dune data

Using the classic `dune` dataset from the `vegan` package:

```{r}
library(vegan)
data(dune)

# Perform NMDS with default settings (Bray-Curtis distance)
nmds <- metaMDS(dune, k = 2, trymax = 100)
nmds
```

This performs Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling on the dune data with:
- `k = 2`: 2 dimensions in the reduced space
- `trymax = 100`: maximum 100 random starting configurations
- Default distance: Bray-Curtis

### Stress value and convergence

```{r}
# Get stress value (lower is better)
nmds$stress

# Stress interpretation:
# < 0.1: Excellent representation
# 0.1-0.2: Good representation
# 0.2-0.3: Fair representation
# > 0.3: Poor representation
```

### NMDS with different distance metrics

```{r}
# Using Jaccard distance (presence-absence)
nmds_jaccard <- metaMDS(dune, distance = "jaccard", k = 2, trymax = 100)
nmds_jaccard$stress

# Using Manhattan distance
nmds_manhattan <- metaMDS(dune, distance = "manhattan", k = 2, trymax = 100)
nmds_manhattan$stress
```

### Basic base R plots

```{r}
# Simple scatter plot of sites
plot(nmds, type = "text", display = "sites",
     main = "NMDS of Dune Sites (Bray-Curtis)")
```

```{r}
# Plot with sites as points and species labels
# Extract coordinates first to avoid argument conflicts
site_coords <- scores(nmds, display = "sites")
species_coords <- scores(nmds, display = "species")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Sites only
plot(site_coords,
     main = "NMDS Sites",
     xlab = "NMDS1", ylab = "NMDS2",
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.5)
abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray")

# Species overlaid on sites
plot(site_coords,
     main = "NMDS Sites with Species",
     xlab = "NMDS1", ylab = "NMDS2",
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.2)
text(species_coords, labels = rownames(species_coords),
     col = "darkgreen", cex = 0.7, font = 2)
abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### Extract and plot coordinates

```{r}
# Extract site coordinates
site_coords <- scores(nmds, display = "sites")
head(site_coords)

# Extract species coordinates
species_coords <- scores(nmds, display = "species")
head(species_coords)
```

### Manual plotting with labels and customization

```{r}
# Custom plot with site labels
plot(site_coords,
     main = "NMDS of Dune Sites",
     xlab = "NMDS1", ylab = "NMDS2",
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.2)
text(site_coords, labels = rownames(dune), pos = 3, cex = 0.7)
abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray")
```

```{r}
# Plot with species trajectories or convex hulls (optional)
plot(site_coords,
     main = "NMDS with Species Vectors",
     xlab = "NMDS1", ylab = "NMDS2",
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.2)
text(site_coords, labels = rownames(dune), pos = 3, cex = 0.7, offset = 0.3)

# Add species points and vectors (species positions)
points(species_coords, pch = 17, col = "darkgreen", cex = 1)
text(species_coords, labels = rownames(species_coords),
     col = "darkgreen", cex = 0.7, offset = 0.3)

abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray")
```

### Shepard plot

```{r}
# Shepard plot: relationship between original distances and ordination distances
plot(nmds$dist, nmds$dists,
     main = "Shepard Plot (NMDS)",
     xlab = "Original Bray-Curtis Distance",
     ylab = "NMDS Distance",
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5)
lines(nmds$dist, nmds$isofit, col = "red", lwd = 2, main = "Isotonic fit")
```

### Key interpretation points

- **Stress value**: Lower is better; typically < 0.2 indicates good representation
- **Shepard plot**: Shows how well the ordination preserves original distances
- **2D vs 3D**: More dimensions reduce stress but increase complexity
- **Distance metric**: Choose based on your data type (Bray-Curtis for abundances, Jaccard for presence-absence)
- **Non-metric**: NMDS preserves rank order of distances, not exact distances
